title: Viability of Singapore Post’s Domestic Post and Parcel Business
what_it_is: Viability of Singapore Post’s Domestic Post and Parcel Business

sections.label: Domestic letter volume decline
sections.summary: Domestic letter volumes fell from around 490 million in FY2015 to 260 million in FY2022 after the COVID-19 pandemic.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: Since the COVID-19 pandemic, the speed and scale of digitalisation has led to a sharp decline in domestic letter volumes, from around 490 million letters in Financial Year (FY) 2015 to just 260 million in FY2022.

sections.label: IMDA review of SingPost
sections.summary: IMDA will work with SingPost to review costs and operations and consider postage rate adjustments to keep its business model viable without direct Government funding.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: The Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA), as the postal regulator, will work with SingPost to review its costs and operations, including optimising and automatic post office services for greater cost effectiveness.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: At the same time, IMDA will consider allowing SingPost to introduce postage rate adjustments in the future to better reflect the cost of letter mail business going forward.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: The upcoming adjustments will have to be of a sufficient degree to allow SingPost's business model to remain viable without requiring direct Government funding.

sections.label: Postal licence conditions
sections.summary: The postal licensee applied for a licence, receives no subsidy, and IMDA imposes conditions including quality of service.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: It means that it applied for a licence to deliver a service in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: So, there is no subsidy to the postal licensee.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: IMDA, as the regulator, imposes certain conditions as part of that licence, and one of the conditions is the quality of service of the licensee.

sections.label: SingPost profitability and segments
sections.summary: The overall company is profitable in its most recent financial statements, and basic postal service is one part of its post and parcel segment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: So, I will not touch on that because it is under the remit of the board and management of the company.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: But I just want to point out that even in its most recent financial statements to its shareholders, the overall company is profitable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: Even in the post and parcel segment of its business, basic postal service or the regulated service, is just one part of that sub-business that it operates.
